text:
Cole Caufield has 12 goals in 20 games and a six-game point streak, and last week he became the first player since Auston Matthews to score 12 goals in a 12-game stretch against Boston, as Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub noted. He's also been in the headlines for calling out the officiating after a controversial penalty call.

The shooting is real. He takes 1.4 expected goals per 60 on his own shots, about what he did last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 97th percentile for chances from the slot. But 12 goals on 8.6 expected is a hot stretch, and Montreal has scored 6.3 more goals than expected with him on the ice. Some of that comes back down. Our talent range still has him around 44 goals for the season.

The counterpoint from Evolving-Hockey: last season he was unlucky, with his chance-based value well ahead of his actual results, against the other team's top players. His wins added on goals this season rank 10th in the league by our count. Watch the five-on-five share, 49% with him on, which is where Montreal's results are outrunning its play.
